subject: Stakeholder mapping & next steps — Hyperion Retail evaluation
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@hyperionretail.com>, Jocelyn Park <jocelyn.park@hyperionretail.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood-inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Stakeholder mapping + next steps (post-call recap)

Hi Samir / Jocelyn —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re all aligned and to make it easy to pull together the stakeholder map you mentioned during the call.

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary use case: customer support summarization + retrieval-augmented responses for chat agents (high query volume, bursty during peak hours)
- Performance targets: p95 latency < 600ms, maintain 99.9% availability for production agents
- Cost sensitivity: looking to optimize token cost for steady-state and peak bursts
- Security requirements: SOC 2 attestation, customer-managed KMS for encryption, VPC peering for private deployments

As discussed, helpful next items from your side so we can route appropriately and estimate timelines:
1) Stakeholder map / org chart showing economic buyer, security/compliance owner, procurement contact, and the engineering owner for integration (we can accept a simple diagram or a list)
2) Any procurement timing or PO templates we should be aware of (expected procurement start date)
3) Decision criteria: top 3 must-haves vs. nice-to-haves (security, latency, cost tradeoffs)
4) Example traffic pattern or sample QPS at peak (if you have a perf spreadsheet that’s ideal)

If easier, feel free to reply with an org chart image and we’ll mark owners in our mutual action plan.

Next steps from Redwood:
- I’ll loop in Rafael (our sales lead) to discuss pricing structure and any potential discounts for an annual commit.
- Laura (CS) will scope an integration checklist and sample evaluation plan.

Proposed timing: If we can get the stakeholder map and procurement contact by next Tuesday (2026-08-10), we’ll prepare a tailored evaluation plan and a draft commercial outline the following week.

Attachment: hyperion-eval-criteria.xlsx (stub)

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com | (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference
From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@hyperionretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Jocelyn Park <jocelyn.park@hyperionretail.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stakeholder mapping + next steps (post-call recap)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Attached is a quick org chart and a spreadsheet with the decision criteria we use for platform purchases.

Attachment: hyperion_org_chart.png (stub)
Attachment: hyperion-decision-criteria.xlsx (stub)

A few clarifications:
- Economic buyer: Amrita Desai (VP, Product) — she’ll want to see unit economics and projected ROI by Q4.
- Security/compliance: Jocelyn is the point for technical security questions; procurement questions should go to procurement@hyperionretail.com.
- Engineering owner: Alex Moran (integration lead) — we’ll intro him once we lock scope.

Procurement timeline: procurement kicks off the vendor review on 2026-09-01; target decision window is mid-September to early October.

I’ll follow up with Alex and procurement and loop them into the thread once I have their OK.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Customer Operations | Hyperion Retail
samir.gupta@hyperionretail.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@hyperionretail.com>, Jocelyn Park <jocelyn.park@hyperionretail.com>, procurement@hyperionretail.com
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood-inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood-inference@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stakeholder mapping + next steps (post-call recap)

Great — really helpful, Samir. Thanks for the org chart and criteria. A couple quick requests so we can tailor our eval plan:

- Can Alex Moran (or you) share a preferred contact / calendaring window for a 30–45 minute technical kickoff (we’ll have Laura join to go over integration checklist)?
- Would procurement be able to share any standard redlines or a PO template ahead of the vendor review? That helps us prepare legal and commercial adjustments proactively.
- For Amrita Desai, would a 1-page ROI summary showing projected monthly token costs + estimated savings from batching/caching be useful? We can prepare that for the executive review.

Rafael — looping you in to give guidance on commercial cadence. Are there pre-approved discount bands for a first-year commit vs. multi-year?

Laura — can you draft a one-page technical evaluation plan (integration checklist + example perf targets) once procurement confirms timelines?

If procurement@hyperionretail.com wants to schedule a short call, we can make time this week or early next week.

Thanks all,
Marissa
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood-inference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Hyperion next steps / discount guidance

Marissa / Laura —

Thanks for the loop. Based on the account size and procurement timeline, we should position:
- Standard annual commit with option to scale in Q1; pricing band: 15–20% discount for a 12-month commit (depending on committed QPS).
- For executive ROI materials: Laura, please include conservative and aggressive cost scenarios (3 and 12-month horizon).

Notes for external: hold off on formal commercial until we have procurement PO template or explicit procurement timeline (their 9/1 vendor review). In parallel, Marissa: prepare the 1-page ROI and sample SOW.

I’ll be ready to jump on a call with procurement if we need quick approvals.

-Rafael
Director, Sales | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood-inference.com
